snippets.description: A simple C++ program that creates a list of numbers and prints them using the modern std::println function.
Uses C++ ranges to filter only even numbers from a list and double each one, like a pipeline of operations.
Defines a concept that only allows number types, then uses it to make an add function that only works with numbers.
A safe divide function that returns either the result or an error message instead of crashing on division by zero.
Looks up a user by ID and returns the user if found, or 'nothing' if the ID is invalid, avoiding null pointer issues.
Adds up all numbers in a collection using span, which works with arrays, vectors, or any contiguous memory.
A 2D point with automatic comparison operators and a method that calculates its distance from the origin.
A coroutine-based generator that can produce values one at a time, pausing and resuming between each one.
Returns different types of values (int, double, or string) from one function using variant as a type-safe union.
Generates the first N Fibonacci numbers using C++ ranges, creating a lazy sequence that computes values on demand.
A memory-safe buffer that automatically cleans up when destroyed. Uses smart pointers so you never forget to free memory.
Checks if a string is a palindrome at compile time, comparing it with its reverse using ranges.
A quicksort that only works with types that can be compared. Uses concepts to enforce this rule at compile time.
Splits a vector into smaller chunks of a given size, like breaking a long list into pages.
A lightweight lock for multithreading that keeps checking until it can acquire access, useful for very short critical sections.
